1.explanation:
- CreateParticipantBehavior.ensureCollaboration: this helper is responsible for turning a lone Process into a Collaboration + Participant when you create the first pool. It calls modeling.makeCollaboration(), which under the hood swaps out the root via UpdateCanvasRootHandler but does not preserve the original process ID on redo.

- UnclaimIdBehavior.preExecute('shape.delete'): when deleting the only Participant, this behavior unclaims the processRef ID, so that when the modeler reverts back to a plain Process root the ID is free and a new one is generated.

- UnclaimIdBehavior.preExecute('canvas.updateRoot'): triggered during root swaps (Process↔Collaboration), it unclaims the old root element’s ID, causing ID churn on delete/undo/redo.

- UpdateCanvasRootHandler: orchestrates the actual root element swap between Process and Collaboration, wiring DI and BPMN definitions. Because it relies on unclaimed IDs, it can trigger fresh ID generation rather than re‐using the old ID.

- BpmnCopyPaste.moddleCopy.canCopyProperty & BpmnCopyPaste.copyPaste.copyElement: these functions manage the deep‐copy of a Participant + its Process on copy/paste. The default behavior copies the entire businessObject, including its ID, leading to duplicate <bpmn:process> IDs in the exported XML.

Together, these classes/functions determine when a process ID is preserved, unclaimed, or copied, and they are therefore the correct places to adjust logic so that:
  • the original process ID is retained on redo of the first participant creation,
  • deleting the last participant does not unclaim the process ID,
  • and copy/paste resets or regenerates the process ID to avoid duplicates.
1.bug_scenario:
There are two related ID‐handling issues in the BPMN modeler:

1. When you add the very first Participant (pool) to an empty diagram, the modeler “re‐uses” the existing Process_1 element by promoting the diagram root to a Collaboration but keeping the process ID. If you undo that addition, the Participant is removed and the process ID remains the same. However when you redo (i.e. add the first Participant again), the process is re‐attached under the new Collaboration with a freshly generated ID instead of the original one.

2. When you delete the only Participant in the model (not via undo, but by simply using delete), the modeler switches the root back from Collaboration to a bare Process. In doing so it unclaims the old process ID, so the new Process gets assigned a new auto‐generated ID.

3. Separately, when copying and pasting an entire Participant (pool) with its underlying Process, the copy/paste logic clones the bpmn:Process and inadvertently reuses the same ID, resulting in two <bpmn:process> elements with identical IDs after export/import.

In short: the modeler is inconsistent about when it reclaims or re‐uses process IDs when moving between Process ↔ Collaboration and when copying pools.

2.explanation:
1. CreateParticipantBehavior (ensureCollaboration): this logic turns the lone Process into a Collaboration and re‐uses the original Process when adding the first Participant. It must preserve the process’s ID on redo, but currently it relies on context.process and oldProcessRef alone.  
2. UnclaimIdBehavior (preExecute 'canvas.updateRoot'): this unclaims the root Process’s ID when the root is updated (i.e. when creating the Collaboration). As a result, on redo the old ID is freed and a new one is generated. Preventing unclaiming in this case (or re-claiming the original ID on redo) will restore consistent IDs.  
3. BpmnCopyPaste (copyPaste.copyElement & copyPaste.pasteElement): when copying/pasting a Pool, the businessObject.id of the underlying Process is copied verbatim into the descriptor and then into the new element. This leads to duplicate <bpmn:process> IDs on import/export. The handlers for copyElement and pasteElement need to omit or regenerate the ‘id’ property so that each pasted Process gets a fresh, unique ID.
2.bug_scenario: The user starts with a blank BPMN model (Process_1) then adds the very first Participant (pool). On “create” the Participant is wrapped in a Collaboration and the original Process is re‐used as the pool’s processRef, keeping its ID. Undoing removes the Participant (and collapses back to the lone Process with its original ID). But Redoing the addition results in the Process getting a brand‐new ID. Separately, when copying and pasting a Pool (with its child Task) the exported/imported XML shows two <bpmn:process> elements with the very same ID, leading to duplicate IDs in the model.
